entries.summary: Use formative and summative evidence to diagnose learning and improve teaching; involve students and account for differences.
Observe engagement, task completion, strategies and language use; give targeted feedback and invite self-correction.
Use varied meaningful tasks, track revision and progress, and assess unit learning processes as well as outcomes.
Combine suitable paper and nonpaper assessment; authentic materials, balanced objective/subjective items and learning portfolios are described.
Plan around curriculum objectives, six content elements and academic quality; choose task types, difficulty and skill proportions explicitly.
Avoid rote and mechanical language-conversion questions; raise integrative/open tasks and strengthen speaking, with authorities determining actual local implementation.
Specify purpose/target, difficulty, task proportions, contexts/tasks, reference answers, scoring criteria and marking methods; assure scientific, fair evaluation.
Separate six-three and five-four versions; use meaningful themes and tasks, genuine varied material and age-appropriate progression.
Develop authentic, diverse and useful curriculum resources beyond textbooks; do not reduce resources to exam drills or increase student burden.
